newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, market seen growing.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, market seen growing.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed with mild losses in blue chips on Tuesday and traders said the market would continue to grow on a higher demand.
"The Croatian market is expanding steadily because of huge demand by foreign investors, banks, companies and funds," Ratko Bubalo of Eastbrokers told Reuters.
"But only annual profit reports will show the level of success (of their investment)," he said.
* Of ten active issues six were up, three down and one flat.
* Biggest gainer, confectioner Kras, jumped 50 kuna to 600 on volume of 315 shares.
* Most actively traded Zagrebacka Banka lost 10 kuna to 1,000 selling 5,250 units.
* Biggest loser was drugs company Pliva, 150 kuna down at 13,000 with 28 shares sold.
* Food processor Podravka rose 10 kuna to 270 and 2,733 shares changed hands.
* Karlovacka Pivovara brewery, last traded in August, gained 15 kuna to 195 on volume of 200 units.
* Three hoteliers were also among gainers:
- Jadranturist by 40 kuna to 340 with 1,290 shares sold.
- Laguna closed 20 kuna up at 920, trading 192 units.
- Arenaturist rose six kuna to 106 selling 2,237 shares.
* Hotelier Riviera lost 10 kuna to 105 and sold 487 shares.
* Another hotelier Suncani Hvar was flat at 45 kuna on volume of 465.
* The second tranche of public debt refinancing bonds traded at 1.04 percent above par, down from 1.07 percent, for 38.4 million kuna turnover. The bonds pay an annual interest of eight percent.
* Turnover higher at 45.8 million, volume also up at 13,197.
